stem.en: A shop adds GST to the price of every item it sells, while an employer takes income tax out of a salary before paying it. Which statement describes the two taxes correctly?

text.en: Income tax is a direct tax, because it is paid directly on the income a person earns.
Income tax is an indirect tax, because its rate is announced by the government every year.
GST is a direct tax, because the shopkeeper hands the collected amount to the government.
GST is an income tax, because it is charged only on the goods a person needs.

explanation.en: The difference is what the tax is charged on, not who hands the money over. Income tax is charged on the income a person earns, so it is direct. GST is charged on the price of a good or service, so it is indirect, even though the shopkeeper collects it and passes it on.

hints.en: Ask what each tax is charged on: the money a person earns, or the price of something they buy?
Who hands the money to the government is not the test. A shopkeeper collects GST from the buyer and passes it on.
